ncert_title: Effects of Physical Activities on Human Body

items.stem: Give one example to show that organ systems work in unison. You may mention two or more organ systems to support your point.
items.answer: Physical activity is a good example, because it is based on motor movements and their co-ordination and needs several organ systems at once. The command for movements comes from the brain, which is a part of the nervous system. The required energy for movements and other activities is obtained from food, and food is completely digested in the intestine, a part of the digestive system. Food and oxygen then reach all the parts of the body through the action of the heart, which is a part of the circulatory system. In fact, many organ systems of the body function as an integrated whole for healthy maintenance of the body.
grounding: For example, physical activities are based on motor movements and their co-ordination.
The command for movements comes from the brain which is a part of the nervous system.
The required energy for movements and other activities is obtained from food.
Food is completely digested in the intestine, a part of digestive system.
Food and oxygen reach all the parts of body through the action of heart, which is a part of the circulatory system.
In fact, many organ systems of the body function as an integrated whole for healthy maintenance of the body.

items.stem: Ravi is a good athlete. Give one permanent effect of being an atlete on of systems his muscular system, and respiratory system.
items.answer: Muscular system: a long term increase in muscle strength, because regular physical exercises increase and maintain strength of muscles; his muscle fibres also enlarge, which causes an overall enlargement of the muscles, and the size of muscles increases by 60 per cent. Respiratory system: an increase in the size of the lungs and the volume of the chest, because physical activity makes more oxygen has to be inhaled, which provides exercise to the lungs and chest so that the size increases and the diaphragm and rib muscles strengthen; exercising regularly also makes vital capacity go upto 5500cc.
grounding: Long term increase in muscle strength: Regular physical exercises increase and maintain strength of muscles.
Muscle fibres enlarge with physical activities which cause an overall enlargement of muscles with the change in its size and shape.
The size of muscles increases by 60 per cent.
Increase in size of lungs and volume of chest: Physical activities require more oxygen.
This provides exercise to the lungs and chest and as a result the size increases.
Simultaneously, the diaphragm and rib muscles strengthen.
Exercising regularly makes vital capacity go upto 5500cc.

items.stem: "Physical activities are necessary for developing a healthy body and healthy mind." Give two examples in support of this statement.
items.answer: A healthy individual is one who has a healthy mind in a healthy body, and performance in any event, sports or otherwise, depends upon physical health as well as mental and emotional health. Example 1 (healthy body): physical activity builds and strengthens muscles, which can protect the bones from injury and support and protect joints from being affected by arthritis, weight bearing exercise helps preserve bone mass and thus protects against osteoporosis, and it is well known that cardiac diseases and high blood pressure can be prevented by regular physical exercises. Example 2 (healthy mind): muscles contract on receiving stimulus from nerves, and the time taken to react to the stimuli, that is reaction time, improves with regular physical exercise, while yogic practice ensures good health and enhances physical fitness.
grounding: You are aware that a healthy individual is one who has a healthy mind in a healthy body.
It is a common experience that performance in any event, sports or otherwise, depends upon physical health, as well as, mental and emotional health.
Physical activity build and strengthen muscles, which can protect the bones from injury, support and protect joints from being affected by arthritis.
Weight bearing exercise helps preserve bone mass and thus protects against osteoporosis (bone degeneration).
It is well known that cardiac diseases and high blood pressure can be prevented by regular physical exercises.
Muscles contract on receiving stimulus from nerves.
The time taken to react to the stimuli (reaction time) improves with regular physical exercise.
Yogic practice ensures good health and enhances physical fitness.

items.stem: Complete the sentence - The respiratory system gets positively affected by undertaking yoga exercises regularly because _____.
items.answer: these asanas develop muscles of the chest, abdomen and lungs and make them active. Muscles of the rib cage are involved in respiration so the asanas indirectly improve respiration.
grounding: It has been found that these asanas develop muscles of the chest, abdomen and lungs and make them active.
Muscles of the rib cage are involved in respiration so the asanas indirectly improve respiration.
Suryanamaskar improves blood circulation and makes the lungs strong.

items.stem: Mention two changes that take place in each of the circulatory and respiratory systems due to regular physical activities.
items.answer: Circulatory system: (i) increase in the size of heart occurs as cardiac muscles develop with regular physical activities, and regular exercise increases the capacity and thickness of the walls of the heart; (ii) decrease in heart rate - under normal conditions the heart beats 72 times per minute at rest, but a trained heart becomes so efficient that at rest same requirement is fulfilled with fewer heartbeats. Respiratory system: (i) increase in the size of the lungs and the volume of the chest, since physical activity provides exercise to the lungs and chest and as a result the size increases; (ii) increase in lung power and vital capacity - respiratory exercises, which include Pranayam and Anulom-vilom, improve lung power, and exercising regularly makes vital capacity go upto 5500cc.
grounding: Increase in the size of heart occurs as cardiac muscles develop with regular physical activities.
Regular exercise increases the capacity and thickness of the walls of the heart.
Decrease in heart rate: Under normal conditions the heart beats 72 times per minute at rest.
heart becomes so efficient that at rest same requirement is fulfilled with fewer heartbeats.

Respiratory exercises, which include Pranayam and Anulom-vilom, improve lung power.
Exercising regularly makes vital capacity go upto 5500cc.
